q: Your definition of AI slop, in one or two sentences, in your own words
a: AI slop is irresponsible use of AI. It is most irresponsible at the design stage where key decisions can be AI-driven, but there should also be examination and validation, even with no record of such validation. I think your following "design decision or implementation detail" is more about the change and not the use of AI. That's exactly what I see here.

q: A change is CRITICAL when it… (tick every condition that is enough on its own)
a: changes a model equation, the topology or a constitutive law, changes a parameter value, a bound or an initial condition, changes data preprocessing (sampling rate, filters, alignment, exclusions), changes what is compared with what, or the comparison metric, can make two code paths silently disagree (fit vs deck, a model vs its copy), states a finding in prose that others will cite, "can make two code paths disagree" is not clear to me. if you mean changing the codepaths of the repo structure, yes this is major.

q: A change counts as EXAMINED when… (tick every condition that is enough on its own)
a: I reproduced its key number another way (hand calculation, a second code path, the paper), I wrote the rationale in my own words (commit message or decision log), A second person reviewed it, I checked it against the source it cites, this does not include all ways to examine. the decision log is good. I would say that creating a workthrough (exercise, tut, or just automatic walkthrough but I must say I followed it) for the next person is also a valid examination. Beyond that, creating no walkthrough and assuming a body of knowledge (eg. currently the case with the filters) assumes that I am either sufficiently knowledgeable to validate on observation, or uninterested in validating due to other constraints. either way, the lack of validation needs to be recognized somehow by the person staging the work.

q: Once examined, is it still slop?
a: No: examined and justified means it is my decision now

q: What should happen to EXAMINED CRITICAL slop?
a: Keep it, with a decision-log entry (the rationale and the check that was done)
